# Vamos UI — site recipes

34 recipes. A recipe says how to build one kind of website from kit components: its pages, what each section is for, the kit items to use (with alternatives), the facts the business supplies, looks that suit it and common pitfalls. There are no example sites to copy. `npx vamos-ui new` (MCP `start_project`) picks the recipe from the interview and keeps only the sections that apply (newsletter, bookings, shop, languages …); MCP `plan_screen` shows the closest recipe for a one-line description.

## academic-department

**Academic department** — A university department, faculty or research institute: masthead with a course search, admissions, research groups, seminars, faculty, a programmes page with a course finder and a people directory.

- `/` **Home**: masthead (`hero` + `input`) → admissions (`table`) → research (`feature-grid`) → events (`list-01`, optional) → faculty (`team`, conditional)
- `/programmes` **Programmes & courses**: intro (`page-intro`) → degrees (`comparison-table`) → finder (`filter-bar` + `accordion` + `progress`) → apply (`steps`)
- `/people` **People**: intro (`page-intro`) → directory (`list-01` + `avatar`)

Looks: corporate serif (theme light, material solid, accent rose, density comfortable, font corporate, radius sharp); research lab (theme light, material solid, accent ocean, density compact, font grotesk).

Pitfalls:
- Course and seat data that goes stale; show when it was last updated and the source.
- Seat meters shown only as bars; give a text value.
- Admission deadlines without time zone or with the wrong academic year.
- Staff emails exposed without the institution's policy, or departed staff still listed.
- Using the university's name or logo against its brand rules.
- A finder that cannot be reached by keyboard or does not announce result counts.

## agency

**Agency or studio** — A creative, digital or brand agency that sells projects and retainers: a statement hero, proof from clients, case studies with measured results, services, how the work runs, the people, and a clear way to start a project. Works for a quiet consultancy-style studio as well as a loud brand studio.

- `/` **Home**: hero (`hero`) → clients (`logo-strip`) → case (`media-text`) → services (`feature-grid`) → work-index (`list-layout`, optional, conditional) → figures (`stats-band`) → process (`steps`) → team (`team`, conditional) → quotes (`testimonials`, conditional) → journal (`blog-list`, conditional) → contact-cta (`cta`)
- `/gallery` **Work** (conditional): intro (`page-intro`) → index (`gallery-section`)
- `/gallery/[slug]` **Case study** (conditional): header (`page-intro`) → story (`rich-text-section`) → system (`gallery-section`) → results (`stats-band`) → quote (`testimonials`, optional) → next (`cta`)
- `/services` **Services** (conditional): intro (`page-intro`) → list (`menu-list`) → faq (`faq`, conditional)
- `/about` **Studio** (conditional): intro (`media-text`) → team (`team`) → careers-cta (`cta`, conditional)
- `/blog` **Journal** (conditional): list (`blog-list`)
- `/contact` **Start a project**: intro (`page-intro`) → brief (`contact-form`) → details (`map-hours`, conditional)

Looks: quiet studio (theme light, material solid, accent graphite, font editorial, density comfortable, radius default); loud brand studio (theme light, material solid, accent brand, font grotesk, density comfortable, radius sharp); dark digital (theme dark, material glass, accent ocean, font grotesk, density comfortable).

Pitfalls:
- Publishing client logos, results or quotes without the client's written permission.
- Results without a period or source ('3x more bookings' with no timeframe) read as invented; give the period and how it was measured.
- Client brand colours used as backgrounds without a contrast check: text on them must stay at least 4.5:1, so route every colour through the accent helper.
- A live 'price' in the brief form that reads like a binding quote; label it as an indicative starting figure and say who confirms it.
- Colour floods, crossfades and scroll effects that ignore prefers-reduced-motion.
- Stock photos of laptops and handshakes instead of the studio's real work and people.
- Case studies that are just image galleries with no problem, approach or outcome.
- Bilingual sites where one language is a weaker translation; both versions must be written with equal care.

## b2b-supplier

**B2B supplier** — A wholesaler, distributor or manufacturer selling to businesses: a catalogue with bulk price tiers or full spec tables, what the plant or warehouse can do, quality and certifications, delivery terms, and a quote request (a quote list with editable lines, or an RFQ form with drawings).

- `/` **Home**: hero (`hero`) → figures (`stats-band`, optional) → catalogue-index (`feature-grid`) → tiers (`pricing-table`, conditional) → capabilities (`media-text` + `feature-grid`) → industries (`feature-grid`, optional) → process (`steps`) → buyers (`testimonials`, optional, conditional) → delivery (`table`) → rfq (`contact-form`, conditional) → plant (`map-hours`, conditional) → faq (`faq`, conditional)
- `/products` **Catalogue**: intro (`page-intro`) → catalogue (`filter-bar` + `data-table`, conditional) → specs (`table` + `tabs`, conditional) → quote-cta (`cta`)
- `/quote` **Quote** (conditional): intro (`page-intro`) → quote-lines (`line-items`) → company-form (`form-01`)
- `/quality` **Quality**: intro (`page-intro`) → process-data (`line-chart` + `stat`, optional) → quality-gates (`steps`) → certificates (`attachment-list`) → faq (`faq`, optional, conditional)

Looks: delivery-note utility (theme light, material solid, accent ocean, density compact, font grotesk, radius sharp); industrial drawing sheet (theme light, material solid, accent graphite, density compact, font corporate, radius sharp); dark plant (theme dark, material solid, accent ember, density compact, font corporate, radius default).

Pitfalls:
- Prices shown without saying whether VAT, shipping and pack size are included.
- Tier charts or drawings with no text equivalent; provide tier prices as a table and drawings with a description.
- Certificates listed without issuing body, scope or valid-until date, or expired ones left online.
- RFQ forms that ask for everything up front; ask for the minimum and say when and who replies.
- Spec tables that overflow on phones without a labelled scroll region or sticky first column.
- Customer logos and quotes used without written permission (common with industrial buyers).
- Privacy notice missing on quote and RFQ forms that collect personal contact data.

## careers

**Careers site** — An employer's careers site: how the company works, what it offers, how hiring runs and who already works there, a searchable board of open roles, and a page per role with a validated application form.

- `/` **Careers**: hero (`hero`) → principles (`media-text`) → numbers (`stats-band`) → benefits (`feature-grid`) → process (`steps`) → voices (`testimonials`, conditional) → latest (`list-layout`) → faq (`faq`, conditional) → cta (`cta`)
- `/careers` **Open roles**: intro (`page-intro`) → board (`filter-bar` + `list-layout`)
- `/careers/[slug]` **Job post**: header (`page-intro`) → description (`rich-text-section`) → apply (`form-01` + `file-upload`) → related (`list-layout`)

Looks: calm and precise (theme light, material solid, accent lime, font grotesk, density comfortable, radius default); corporate employer (theme light, material solid, accent ocean, font corporate, density comfortable).

Pitfalls:
- Discriminatory wording in job posts (age, gender, nationality) or asking for a photo, marital status or date of birth; many jurisdictions forbid it.
- Collecting CVs without a candidate privacy notice, retention period and an unticked consent box.
- Closed roles left on the board; every role needs a closing date and is removed after it.
- No salary band: candidates skip roles without one, and some markets require it.
- File upload without clear format and size limits, or errors shown only in colour.
- Filter results and counts that change silently; announce them in a status region.
- Stock photos of smiling strangers instead of real colleagues and workplaces.

## community-forum

**Community forum** — A forum or community home: live counters, the latest discussions with activity, categories, meetups and top helpers, a topics list with sorting and paging, and solved threads with replies.

- `/` **Home**: header (`page-header` + `stat`) → latest (`list-01` + `sparkline` + `avatar`) → categories (`list-01`) → meetups (`list-01`, optional) → helpers (`avatar` + `list-01`, optional)
- `/topics` **All topics**: list (`list-01` + `sparkline` + `pagination`)
- `/t/[slug]` **Thread**: title (`page-header`) → posts (`comment-thread`) → pulse (`description-list` + `avatar`)

Looks: dense workshop (theme light, material solid, accent ember, density compact, font system, radius default); dark developer (theme dark, material solid, accent lime, density compact, font grotesk).

Pitfalls:
- Sparklines and counters without text equivalents.
- Heavy motion on a reading-heavy site; keep transitions quick and honour reduced motion.
- No visible guidelines, reporting or moderation path.
- Showing members' real names, emails or locations without consent.
- An empty-looking launch; seed real topics and answers before going live.
- Live counters ('online now') that are fake or never update.

## conference

**Conference** — A conference, summit or festival site: dates and venue up front, speakers, a multi-day schedule with tracks and a personal agenda, sponsors and a tickets page with tiers and the code of conduct.

- `/` **Home**: hero (`hero` + `countdown`) → speakers (`team`) → programme-glance (`tabs` + `feature-grid`) → venue (`map-hours`) → sponsors (`logo-strip`, optional) → tickets-cta (`cta`) → faq (`faq`, optional, conditional)
- `/schedule` **Schedule**: intro (`page-intro`) → board (`tabs` + `activity-timeline` + `button-group`)
- `/tickets` **Tickets**: intro (`page-intro`) → tiers (`pricing-table`) → included (`comparison-table`) → conduct (`rich-text-section`) → ticket-faq (`faq`)

Looks: poster grotesk (theme light, material solid, accent ember, density compact, font grotesk, radius sharp); night programme (theme dark, material solid, accent lime, density compact, font grotesk); formal summit (theme light, material solid, accent ocean, density comfortable, font corporate, radius default).

Pitfalls:
- The countdown is the only place the date appears; always print the dates and time zone as text.
- Schedule tracks distinguished by colour alone; add labels or glyphs.
- Agenda saved only in the browser without saying so; tell attendees it is stored on this device.
- Ticket prices shown without saying whether tax and fees are included, or without refund and transfer terms.
- No code of conduct or no way to report an incident during the event.
- Venue accessibility missing or vague (step-free routes, seating, captions).
- Speakers listed before they have confirmed; mark the programme as provisional until it is final.

## contractor

**Contractor or builder** — A building contractor, developer or construction firm: completed and ongoing projects with their progress, the services and sectors it builds for, safety record, how it runs a site, the people, and a tender or project enquiry.

- `/` **Home**: hero (`hero`) → figures (`stats-band`) → projects (`entity-card`, conditional) → services (`feature-grid`) → safety (`media-text`) → method (`steps`) → people (`team`, conditional) → clients (`testimonials`, conditional) → faq (`faq`, conditional) → enquiry (`contact-form`) → offices (`map-hours`, conditional)
- `/projects` **Projects** (conditional): intro (`page-intro`) → list (`filter-bar` + `entity-card`)
- `/projects/[slug]` **Project** (conditional): intro (`page-intro`) → facts (`description-list`) → timeline (`gantt`) → gallery (`gallery-section`, optional) → more (`entity-card`)
- `/services` **Services** (conditional): intro (`page-intro`) → list (`media-text`) → cta (`cta`)
- `/contact` **Contact**: form (`contact-form`) → offices (`map-hours`)

Looks: site hoarding (theme light, material glass, accent ember, font grotesk, density comfortable, radius sharp); engineering dark (theme dark, material solid, accent graphite, font corporate, density compact).

Pitfalls:
- Safety figures without period and source, or certifications that have expired.
- Naming clients or showing their logos without permission, especially on public tenders with disclosure rules.
- Progress timelines left stale; if the diary is not updated, hide the timeline rather than show old progress as current.
- Draggable timelines that only work with a mouse; provide buttons and arrow keys.
- Hazard-tape and pouring animations that ignore reduced motion.
- Photos of other firms' buildings or generic stock cranes; use the firm's own sites.
- Missing contractor registration or licence details where the market requires them.

## developer-tool

**Developer tool / API** — Site for an API, SDK, CLI or other developer product: a code-first hero, a quick start with code per step, measured reliability, usage-based pricing with an estimator, a docs landing with search and SDKs, and a changelog. Code samples follow one language choice across the whole site.

- `/` **Home**: hero (`hero` + `tabs` + `kbd`) → quickstart (`steps` + `tabs`) → features (`feature-grid`) → reliability (`stats-band`) → pricing (`pricing-table` + `slider`, conditional) → faq (`faq`, conditional) → closing-cta (`cta`)
- `/docs` **Docs**: intro (`page-intro` + `command`) → guides (`feature-grid`) → first-request (`tabs`) → sdks (`table`)
- `/changelog` **Changelog**: intro (`page-intro`) → recent (`release-notes`) → full-log (`cta`, optional)

Looks: graphite compact code (theme light, material solid, accent graphite, density compact, font grotesk, radius sharp); dark terminal (theme dark, material solid, accent ocean, density compact, font system).

Pitfalls:
- Code shown as images or with smart quotes from a word processor; samples must be selectable, copyable and actually run.
- Language tabs that only switch one window; one choice should drive every sample, install line and SDK row.
- Copy buttons that fail silently where the clipboard API is blocked; provide a fallback and announce the result.
- Uptime or latency claims that do not match the public status page.
- Usage pricing without a worked example or estimator; developers leave when they cannot predict the bill.
- Docs search reachable only by mouse; support '/' to focus, arrows and Enter, and keep a skip link.
- Breaking changes buried in release notes without an upgrade note and a date.

## digital-products

**Digital products shop** — A shop selling downloadable products such as templates, themes, UI kits, presets, fonts, e-books or courses: a shelf with live or real previews, licence tiers, a product page with preview and changelog, and a checkout that ends in a download and licence key.

- `/` **Home**: hero (`hero`) → shelf (`filter-bar` + `feature-grid`) → whats-inside (`feature-grid`) → licences (`comparison-table`, conditional) → reviews (`testimonials`, optional, conditional) → faq (`faq`, conditional) → newsletter (`cta`, conditional)
- `/products/[slug]` **Product**: preview (`product-01`) → details (`description-list`) → changelog (`release-notes`)
- `/checkout` **Checkout**: checkout (`checkout-01`)
- `/order/[id]` **Download**: confirmation (`order-confirmation-01`)

Looks: precise tool (theme light, material glass, accent lime, density comfortable, font grotesk, radius default); dark studio (theme dark, material solid, accent ocean, density compact, font grotesk, radius sharp); quiet editorial (theme light, material solid, accent graphite, density comfortable, font editorial, radius default).

Pitfalls:
- Licence terms vague ('commercial use allowed') instead of concrete rows: seats, projects, client work, resale.
- Right of withdrawal not handled: consumers must explicitly agree that the download starts immediately and waives withdrawal.
- Total changes at the last step because tax by country is added late; ask the billing country early.
- Previews that are only images with no text description, or live previews full of headings and landmarks that confuse screen readers.
- Download links that expire without a way to get them again.
- Changelog missing or stale, which makes buyers doubt the product is maintained.
- Live previews that load a whole app on the home page and slow it down; freeze thumbnails, run the live one only on demand.

## game

**Game** — Site for a video game (often from a small studio): key art and a click-to-load trailer, press quotes, game pillars, a facts ledger, screenshots, a dev diary and a launch email; a media page with every trailer and a screenshot mosaic; and a press kit with a fact sheet, copy-ready texts and downloads.

- `/` **Home**: hero (`hero` + `video-player`) → press-quotes (`testimonials`, optional) → pillars (`media-text`) → facts (`description-list`) → screens (`gallery-section` + `lightbox`) → diary (`blog-list`, conditional) → wishlist (`cta`, conditional)
- `/media` **Media**: intro (`page-intro`) → trailers (`video-player`) → screenshots (`gallery-section` + `lightbox`)
- `/press` **Press kit**: intro (`page-intro`) → fact-sheet (`description-list` + `rich-text-section`) → downloads (`attachment-list` + `checkbox`) → team (`team`, conditional) → keys (`contact-form`) → press-faq (`faq`)

Looks: dark heavy display (theme dark, material glass, accent ember, density comfortable, font grotesk, radius sharp); bright playful (theme light, material solid, accent rose, density comfortable, font grotesk, radius round).

Pitfalls:
- Autoplaying or eagerly embedded trailers that load third-party players and cookies before the visitor presses play.
- Trailers without captions, and screenshots with empty alt text.
- Age rating, platforms or release date missing or out of date across pages.
- A press kit that needs an email to get assets; journalists leave.
- Store badges and platform logos used against the platform's brand rules.
- Launch email signups without consent text or with a newsletter the visitor did not ask for.
- Flashing effects in key art or trailers without a warning; respect reduced motion.

## home-services

**Home and local services** — A local service business that prices by the job and works by appointment: moving, cleaning, repairs, installation, car service or washing. The site's core is an instant quote calculator or a service picker that shows price and time live, a price list, a booking or quote request, trust signals (insurance, warranty, crew) and a searchable FAQ.

- `/` **Home**: hero (`hero`) → proof (`stats-band`) → picker (`capacity-finder`, conditional) → services (`menu-list`) → combo (`media-text`, optional) → day (`steps`) → team (`team`, conditional) → reviews (`testimonials`, conditional) → faq (`faq`, conditional) → locations (`map-hours`, conditional) → cta (`cta`)
- `/services` **Prices and times** (conditional): intro (`page-intro`) → list (`menu-list`)
- `/quote` **Get a quote** (conditional): intro (`page-intro`) → calculator (`multi-step-form`)
- `/booking` **Book** (conditional): intro (`page-intro`) → flow (`scheduler`)
- `/faq` **FAQ** (conditional): intro (`page-intro`) → answers (`faq` + `filter-bar`) → cta (`cta`)
- `/contact` **Contact**: form (`contact-form`) → locations (`map-hours`, conditional)

Looks: trusty blue (theme light, material glass, accent ocean, font corporate, density comfortable, radius default); workshop dark (theme dark, material solid, accent brand, font grotesk, density compact, radius sharp); fresh and friendly (theme light, material solid, accent lime, font system, density comfortable, radius round).

Pitfalls:
- Calculator prices that do not match the price list or the final invoice; derive both from one pricing model and state the assumptions behind 'from' prices.
- A live estimate presented as a fixed price; show a range, state what can change it (access, extra items) and who confirms it.
- Hidden surcharges (weekend, month-end, distance, VAT) that only appear on the invoice; show them as line items in the estimate.
- Insurance and warranty claims without the cover amount, insurer or terms.
- Booking calendars that offer closed days or full slots, or have no cancellation policy.
- Multi-step forms that lose answers on going back or on a language switch, or do not announce step changes and live totals to screen readers.
- Long forms on mobile with tiny segmented controls; keep touch targets large and let people call instead.
- Collecting addresses and phone numbers without a privacy notice.

## launch-waitlist

**Launch waitlist** — A pre-launch page for a product (or event) that is not live yet: one promise, one validated email form, a countdown to the opening, a few proof points and a 'you're on the list' state with a referral link that moves the person up the line.

- `/` **Home**: hero (`hero` + `countdown`) → why (`feature-grid`) → faq (`faq`, optional)
- `/joined` **You're on the list**: position (`stat` + `progress`, optional) → share (`input` + `button`, optional) → next (`steps`)

Looks: soft editorial glass (theme light, material glass, accent brand, density comfortable, font editorial, radius round); dark launch countdown (theme dark, material glass, accent ember, density comfortable, font grotesk).

Pitfalls:
- A countdown that reaches zero with nothing live; update the page or switch it to 'out now' before the date.
- Countdowns without a time zone, or that cause hydration mismatches and read every second to screen readers.
- Collecting emails without consent text, double opt-in or a privacy link.
- Fake waiting-list numbers or positions; only show counts that are real.
- Validation errors not tied to the input, or an error shown before the person typed anything.
- More than one call to action; the page has one job.
- Referral schemes that promise rewards the business cannot deliver at launch.

## local-shop

**Local made-to-order shop** — A local shop that makes goods to order and delivers them the same or next day in its area: a seasonal catalogue, delivery areas with fees and cut-off times, and an order form whose delivery date follows the area and the clock. Fits florists, gift shops, cake and made-to-order bakery shops and similar.

- `/` **Home**: hero (`hero`) → seasonal-edit (`feature-grid`) → principles (`feature-grid`, optional) → subscriptions (`pricing-table`, optional, conditional) → delivery-areas (`table`) → shop (`map-hours`, conditional) → faq (`faq`, optional, conditional)
- `/products` **Catalogue**: intro (`page-intro`) → catalogue (`filter-bar` + `feature-grid`)
- `/place-order` **Order**: order-form (`multi-step-form` + `calendar`)
- `/contact` **Contact** (conditional): contact (`contact-form`)

Looks: soft magazine (theme light, material glass, accent rose, density comfortable, font editorial, radius round); warm bakery counter (theme light, material solid, accent ember, density comfortable, font editorial, radius default); fresh local (theme light, material solid, accent lime, density comfortable, font system, radius round).

Pitfalls:
- Cut-off shown only as a ticking clock; screen readers and quick readers need it as text, and it must use the shop's time zone, not the visitor's.
- Calendar allowing dates the shop cannot deliver (closed days, past cut-off, too far ahead, areas without same-day delivery).
- Delivery fees hidden until checkout; show the area table on the home page.
- No substitution policy for seasonal items that run out, leading to disputes.
- Recipient phone and address collected without saying why or how long they are kept (privacy notice required).
- Card message preview with no character limit or one that differs from the printed card.
- Motion (swinging tags, blurred fades) not stopped for reduced motion.

## marketplace

**Marketplace** — A multi-seller marketplace where buyers search listings from many independent sellers and choose by seller reputation: search-first home, results with filters (seller rating, category, price, dispatch time), seller pages with ratings and reviews, and a call for new sellers.

- `/` **Home**: hero (`hero`) → categories (`feature-grid`) → top-sellers (`entity-card`) → new-listings (`feature-grid`) → how-buying-works (`steps`) → figures (`stats-band`, optional) → sell-cta (`cta`) → faq (`faq`, conditional)
- `/search` **Search results**: results (`filter-bar` + `list-layout`)
- `/sellers/[slug]` **Seller**: seller-header (`page-header`) → seller-tabs (`tabs` + `feature-grid` + `testimonials`)
- `/products/[slug]` **Listing**: product (`product-01`) → more-from-seller (`feature-grid`)
- `/cart` **Cart**: cart (`cart-01`)
- `/checkout` **Checkout**: checkout (`checkout-01`)
- `/order/[id]` **Order confirmation**: confirmation (`order-confirmation-01`)

Looks: trustworthy marketplace (theme light, material glass, accent ocean, density comfortable, font system, radius default); dense catalogue (theme light, material solid, accent graphite, density compact, font system, radius sharp).

Pitfalls:
- Buyers cannot see who the actual seller is (name, legal identity, location) before paying — required for consumer protection and trust.
- Ratings without the evidence behind them (count, recency, on-time share) or badges whose rule is not explained.
- Filter counts that do not match the results, or filters lost when the language changes.
- Phone filter sheet that does not return focus to its trigger, and toggles without aria-pressed.
- Shipping and returns unclear when one order has items from several sellers.
- Fake or seeded reviews; only show reviews from completed orders.
- Seller onboarding page missing fees and payout timing.

## mobile-app

**Mobile app** — Landing site for a launched iOS / Android app: phone mockups in the hero, a feature walkthrough where the phone screen changes as you scroll, a hands-on planner or plan tabs, store reviews, pricing for in-app plans, a download page and, for apps that hold money or personal data, a security page. Works for playful consumer apps and calm, trust-first finance or utility apps.

- `/` **Home**: hero (`hero`) → trust (`feature-grid`, optional) → features (`section-nav` + `media-text`) → numbers (`stats-band`, optional) → try-it (`tabs`, optional) → reviews (`testimonials`, conditional) → faq (`faq`, conditional) → closing-cta (`cta`)
- `/pricing` **Pricing** (conditional): intro (`page-intro`) → plans (`pricing-table`) → compare (`comparison-table`) → billing-faq (`faq`)
- `/download` **Download**: get (`media-text` + `qr-code`) → setup (`steps`) → faq (`faq`)
- `/security` **Security**: intro (`page-intro`) → layers (`feature-grid`) → health (`uptime-bars`, optional) → lost-phone (`steps`) → report (`rich-text-section`)

Looks: dark energetic glass (theme dark, material glass, accent lime, density comfortable, font grotesk, radius round); calm trusted light (theme light, material glass, accent ocean, density comfortable, font corporate, radius default).

Pitfalls:
- Fake or unlicensed store badges and device frames; use the official artwork and its rules.
- Phone screens as unlabelled images; label each with what the screen shows.
- Scroll-driven phones that break on small screens or under reduced motion; repeat screens inline and swap without animation.
- Projections and interest rates presented as promises; label them illustrative, date them and add the regulatory disclaimer.
- Regulated apps missing licence / regulator details or deposit-protection wording in the footer.
- Ratings and review quotes without source, count and date.
- Prices that differ from the in-store price or omit how to cancel a store subscription.

## musician

**Musician or band** — A site for a band, musician, DJ or performer built around the new release and the tour: tour dates with ticket states, a discography with tracklists, videos, merch and a mailing list for presale codes.

- `/` **Home**: hero (`hero`) → release (`media-text` + `table`) → tour-preview (`fixture-list` + `badge`) → videos (`video-player`, optional) → merch (`entity-card`, optional, conditional) → mailing-list (`form-01`, conditional)
- `/tour` **Tour**: intro (`page-intro`) → dates (`fixture-list` + `filter-bar` + `switch`) → faq (`faq`)
- `/music` **Music**: intro (`page-intro`) → discography (`gallery` + `filter-bar` + `table`) → band (`team`, optional)
- `/contact` **Contact** (conditional): contacts (`description-list`) → press-kit (`attachment-list`, optional) → form (`contact-form`, conditional)

Looks: loud poster (theme dark, material solid, density compact, font grotesk, accent rose, radius sharp); quiet record sleeve (theme light, material solid, density comfortable, font editorial, accent graphite, radius sharp).

Pitfalls:
- Ticket state shown by colour alone; 'sold out', 'few left' and 'new date' must be written, and moved shows must show both dates.
- Out-of-date tour lists: past dates should drop off or move to an archive automatically.
- Embedding video players that load third-party trackers on page load; use a click-to-load facade and mention it in the privacy notice.
- Mailing-list signup without explicit consent, a privacy link or a clear cadence.
- Text over a busy hero photo without a scrim fails contrast; placeholder alt text left on the hero photo.
- Auto-moving tickers or animations with no pause control and no reduced-motion fallback.
- External ticket and store links that open a new tab without saying so.

## newsletter-writer

**Writer's newsletter** — An email-first publication by one writer or a small desk: the subscribe form is the hero, the latest letter proves the voice, a searchable archive and single-issue pages do the rest.

- `/` **Home**: nameplate (`hero` + `form-01`) → recent (`list-layout`) → about (`media-text`) → readers (`testimonials`, optional, conditional) → faq (`faq`, conditional)
- `/archive` **Archive**: intro (`page-intro`) → search (`filter-bar` + `input` + `list-layout`) → subscribe (`form-01`)
- `/archive/[slug]` **Letter**: letter (`article-layout`) → subscribe (`form-01`) → neighbours (`pagination`)

Looks: slow desk (theme light, material solid, density comfortable, font editorial, accent ember, radius sharp); briefing (theme light, material solid, density compact, font grotesk, accent ocean, radius default).

Pitfalls:
- Signup without double opt-in, explicit consent or a privacy link; say what is sent and how often next to the button.
- Inflated or stale subscriber counts; show a count only if it is true and kept current.
- Subscribe success that is not announced to screen readers, or a typo hint not linked to the email field.
- An archive search that misses words written with or without diacritics.
- Letters only available in the inbox: every issue should have its own page and stay linkable.
- Reader quotes used without permission or attributed to full names that readers did not agree to show.

## nonprofit

**Non-profit** — A charity, foundation or community project that raises one-off and monthly donations: mission and current campaign, what each gift buys, programmes, stories, a donate page and a transparency report.

- `/` **Home**: hero (`hero` + `progress`) → impact (`stats-band`) → give (`button-group` + `card`) → programmes (`feature-grid`) → stories (`testimonials`, optional, conditional) → how-it-works (`steps`) → volunteer (`cta`) → newsletter (`cta`, conditional)
- `/donate` **Donate**: intro (`page-intro` + `progress`) → amount (`button-group` + `card`) → details (`form-01`) → next (`steps`) → faq (`faq`)
- `/transparency` **Transparency report**: intro (`page-intro`) → figures (`stats-band`) → split (`donut-chart`) → ledger (`table`) → files (`attachment-list`) → board (`team`, optional, conditional) → cta (`cta`)

Looks: warm report (theme light, material solid, accent rose, density comfortable, font editorial, radius sharp); plain civic (theme light, material solid, accent ocean, density comfortable, font system).

Pitfalls:
- Impact numbers without a year or source read as marketing; always date and source them.
- The gift visualisation carries the meaning; keep the itemised amounts as text and mark drawings decorative.
- Tax-deduction or receipt claims that do not match the organisation's legal status.
- Photos of children or vulnerable people without consent, or with identifying details.
- Monthly gifts without a clear way to change or cancel.
- No transparency report or files, or figures that do not add up to the totals.
- Marketing consent bundled into the donation; keep updates opt-in.

## online-course

**Online course** — An online course, bootcamp or cohort programme: outcome-first home, who it is for, a curriculum map with weekly pace, student projects, instructor, cohort dates, pricing and an enrol form.

- `/` **Home**: announcement (`announcement-bar`, optional) → hero (`hero`) → fit (`feature-grid`) → map (`progress` + `slider` + `button-group`) → projects (`card`, optional, conditional) → instructor (`media-text`) → dates (`calendar` + `radio-group`) → pricing (`pricing-table`, conditional) → faq (`faq`)
- `/curriculum` **Curriculum**: intro (`page-intro`) → map (`progress` + `slider`) → modules (`accordion`) → cta (`cta`)
- `/enrol` **Instructor & enrol**: intro (`page-intro`) → story (`media-text`) → mentors (`team`, optional, conditional) → how (`steps`) → form (`form-01` + `calendar` + `radio-group`)

Looks: ink and mustard (theme light, material solid, accent ember, density compact, font editorial, radius sharp); dark bootcamp (theme dark, material glass, accent lime, density compact, font grotesk).

Pitfalls:
- Outcome or salary claims without evidence.
- Live session times without a time zone.
- Refund, cancellation and withdrawal rights missing near the price.
- A curriculum map that only works by dragging; keep the module list as text.
- Student projects or quotes published without consent.
- 'Certificate' implied to be accredited when it is not.

## online-store

**Online store** — A brand selling its own physical products online: a home page that sells one hero product and the range, a filterable product listing, product detail with variants, cart and checkout. Also covers shops that sell in timed, limited drops (countdown, locked previews, stock against the run).

- `/` **Home**: shipping-notice (`announcement-bar`, optional) → hero (`hero`) → locked-preview (`entity-card` + `feature-grid`, optional) → categories (`feature-grid`) → new-in (`carousel`) → maker-story (`media-text`, optional, conditional) → lookbook (`gallery-section`, optional, conditional) → drop-rules (`steps`, optional) → reviews (`testimonials`, optional, conditional) → faq (`faq`, optional, conditional) → newsletter (`cta`, conditional)
- `/products` **Shop**: intro (`page-intro`) → listing (`filter-bar` + `pagination`)
- `/products/[slug]` **Product**: product (`product-01`) → reviews (`testimonials`, optional, conditional) → related (`feature-grid`)
- `/cart` **Cart**: cart (`cart-01`)
- `/checkout` **Checkout**: checkout (`checkout-01`)
- `/order/[id]` **Order confirmation**: confirmation (`order-confirmation-01`)

Looks: warm editorial craft (theme light, material solid, accent ember, density comfortable, font editorial, radius default); dark dense drop (theme dark, material solid, accent rose, density compact, font grotesk, radius sharp); clean neutral retail (theme light, material solid, accent graphite, density comfortable, font system, radius default).

Pitfalls:
- Missing distance-sales contract, pre-information form and returns policy at checkout (legally required for consumer sales in many markets).
- Only one photo per product while variant swatches promise more; every swatch must swap to a real photo of that variant.
- Prices shown without VAT or shipping until the last step; show the free-delivery threshold and shipping early.
- Cart lost on language or currency switch; keep it in a store above the locale switch.
- Swatches and size buttons that are colour-only or mouse-only; use labelled radiogroups / aria-pressed and name sold-out sizes.
- Countdowns that announce every second to screen readers or animate without honouring reduced motion.
- Cart drawer that does not trap focus or return it to the cart button when closed.
- Stock numbers that are not real; fake scarcity erodes trust and can breach consumer law.

## personal-cv

**Personal site and CV** — A one-page personal site for an engineer, designer, consultant or freelancer, with numbered sections and a sticky identity column, plus the same content as a print-perfect A4 CV that saves as PDF.

- `/` **Home**: identity (`section-nav` + `badge` + `button`) → about (`typography`) → experience (`activity-timeline`) → projects (`list-layout` + `badge`, optional) → writing (`blog-list`, optional, conditional) → skills (`description-list`) → contact (`description-list` + `button`)
- `/cv` **CV**: toolbar (`button`) → sheet (`description-list` + `typography`)

Looks: plain engineer (theme light, material solid, density compact, font system, accent ocean, radius default); editorial profile (theme light, material solid, density comfortable, font editorial, accent graphite, radius sharp).

Pitfalls:
- Printing the whole site instead of the CV: hide site chrome in print and print only the sheet, on A4 with real margins.
- Dark mode leaking into the printed or on-screen CV sheet; keep the paper light and check it reads without colour.
- Content that breaks across pages mid-entry; avoid breaks inside entries and keep the reading order logical when printed.
- Publishing a full home address, date of birth, ID number or a personal phone number the person did not mean to make public.
- Links that print as 'here': print the address itself so the PDF stays useful on paper.
- The sticky identity column taking the whole screen on phones; it should stack above the content there.
- Section navigation without aria-current, or scroll effects that ignore reduced motion.

## podcast

**Podcast** — A site for a podcast or audio show: the newest episode in a player on the home page, a searchable episode archive, the hosts, follow links and guest suggestions, and an episode page with chapters, a synced transcript and show notes.

- `/` **Home**: hero (`hero` + `audio-player`) → episodes (`accordion` + `filter-bar` + `input`) → hosts (`team`) → how-made (`media-text`, optional) → follow (`cta`) → suggest (`contact-form`, optional, conditional)
- `/episodes` **Episodes** (conditional): intro (`page-intro`) → list (`accordion` + `filter-bar` + `pagination`)
- `/episodes/[slug]` **Episode**: intro (`page-intro`) → player (`audio-player`) → notes (`tabs` + `accordion` + `description-list`) → more (`blog-list`)

Looks: late-night studio (theme dark, material glass, density comfortable, font grotesk, accent ember, radius round); radio bulletin (theme light, material solid, density compact, font corporate, accent ocean, radius default).

Pitfalls:
- No transcript: publish one per episode (accessibility and search), synced or at least timestamped.
- A scrubber or waveform that only works with a mouse; it must be a keyboard slider with an accessible name and value.
- Live regions that announce every caption line over the audio; keep the spoken-line caption silent to screen readers.
- Autoplaying audio on page load.
- Episode pages without the audio file, date and duration, or a broken RSS feed link.
- Third-party player embeds that load trackers before the visitor presses play.
- Guest suggestion form without a privacy note, collecting more than needed.

## portfolio-studio

**Portfolio or creative studio** — A work-led site for a photographer, architecture / interiors / design practice or photo studio: the work leads, each project gets its own case page, and an about + contact page closes the sale. Studios that sell fixed packages add a pricing page with a package builder and a booking page.

- `/` **Home**: hero (`hero`) → selected-work (`gallery` + `tabs` + `lightbox`) → project-index (`table` + `filter-bar`, optional) → practice (`feature-grid` + `stats-band`, optional, conditional) → studio-kit (`feature-grid`, optional, conditional) → packages (`pricing-table`, conditional) → recognition (`list-layout`, optional) → team (`team`, optional, conditional) → bio-cta (`cta`)
- `/gallery` **Work** (conditional): intro (`page-intro`) → wall (`gallery` + `tabs` + `lightbox`) → index (`table` + `filter-bar`)
- `/projects/[slug]` **Project**: intro (`page-intro` + `description-list`) → cover (`image`) → story (`feature-grid`) → series (`gallery` + `lightbox`, optional) → credits (`description-list`, optional) → next (`cta`)
- `/pricing` **Packages** (conditional): intro (`page-intro`) → presets (`pricing-table`) → builder (`radio-group` + `slider` + `checkbox` + `line-items`)
- `/booking` **Booking** (conditional): intro (`page-intro`) → slot (`calendar`) → details (`form-01`) → summary (`line-items`)
- `/about` **About**: intro (`page-intro`) → approach (`media-text`) → team (`team`, conditional) → process (`steps`, optional) → clients-shows (`list-layout`, optional) → visit (`map-hours`, conditional) → faq (`faq`, conditional) → contact (`contact-form`, conditional)

Looks: type-led gallery (theme light, material solid, density compact, font grotesk, accent ember, radius sharp); drawing sheet (theme light, material solid, density comfortable, font corporate, accent ocean, radius sharp); darkroom mono (theme light, material solid, density compact, font grotesk, accent graphite, radius sharp).

Pitfalls:
- Every image needs meaningful alt text; the lightbox must trap focus, close on Escape and return focus to the image that opened it.
- Hover-only effects (cursor-following cover previews, hover captions) must have a keyboard and touch equivalent; the project list stays usable as plain links.
- Huge unoptimised images: give width and height, serve sized variants and only prioritise the hero.
- Showing client names, logos or recognisable people without permission or a model release; state image licensing terms rather than implying images are free to use.
- Prices shown without VAT or without saying what is included, and deposits without refund and reschedule terms next to the button.
- A live quote that is not announced: put the total in a polite status region and keep it in sync with the booking summary.
- Category filters that hide everything or lose state on language switch; show counts and keep the choice.
- Decorative extras (grid overlays, keyboard shortcuts) presented as if required to use the site.

## product-support

**Product support site (help centre, changelog, status)** — The companion sites of a software product: a help centre with instant search, categories and articles; a changelog with release filters and subscribe; and a public status page with components, uptime bars, incidents and history. Each part is independent: build only the parts the business runs (often each on its own subdomain), and treat the first page of each part as its home.

- `/` **Help centre**: search (`command` + `hero`) → topics (`feature-grid`) → popular (`list-layout`) → contact (`feature-grid` + `contact-form`)
- `/help/[slug]` **Help category**: intro (`page-intro`) → articles (`list-layout` + `input`)
- `/help/article/[slug]` **Help article**: article (`article-layout`) → helpful (`feedback-prompt`) → related (`list-layout` + `cta`)
- `/changelog` **Changelog**: masthead (`page-intro`) → releases (`release-notes`) → subscribe (`cta`, conditional)
- `/changelog/[slug]` **Release**: entry (`article-layout`) → more (`pagination` + `cta`)
- `/status` **Status**: now (`alert` + `activity-timeline`) → components (`uptime-bars`) → performance (`bar-chart` + `list-layout`, optional) → subscribe (`cta`)
- `/status/incidents/[id]` **Incident**: summary (`description-list` + `card`) → updates (`activity-timeline`) → postmortem (`rich-text-section`, optional)
- `/status/history` **Incident history**: intro (`page-intro`) → list (`filter-bar` + `list-layout`)

Looks: calm civic help (theme light, material solid, accent ocean, density comfortable, font system, radius default); narrow editorial notes (theme light, material solid, accent ocean, density comfortable, font editorial); neutral compact status (theme light, material solid, accent graphite, density compact, font system, radius sharp).

Pitfalls:
- A status page hosted on the same infrastructure as the product goes down with it; host it separately.
- Status colour as the only signal, or coloured small text that fails contrast; pair every state with a word and an icon.
- Uptime bars that cannot be read by keyboard or screen reader; give each day a tooltip and a text alternative.
- Incident times without a time zone, or incidents quietly removed from history.
- Help search that needs Enter and a results page, or misses words with diacritics.
- Articles without an updated date or with steps as prose instead of an ordered list.
- Changelog entries without real dates, or breaking changes without an upgrade note.
- Subscribe forms without a confirmation state and clear consent for what will be sent.

## professional-firm

**Professional firm** — A law, accounting, tax, audit or advisory practice: sober and trustworthy, organised around practice areas or service packages run by named partners, with credentials, an approach, insights, transparent fees where the profession allows, and an enquiry that respects confidentiality.

- `/` **Home**: hero (`hero`) → figures (`stats-band`, optional) → practices (`feature-grid`) → fee-preview (`pricing-table`, conditional) → approach (`steps`) → partners (`team`, conditional) → switching (`media-text`, optional) → reviews (`testimonials`, conditional) → insights (`blog-list`, conditional) → faq (`faq`, conditional) → enquiry (`contact-form`)
- `/services` **Practice areas**: intro (`page-intro`) → list (`menu-list`) → fee-estimate (`form-01`, conditional) → faq (`faq`, conditional)
- `/services/[slug]` **Practice area**: intro (`page-intro`) → scope (`feature-grid`) → matters (`description-list`) → lead (`media-text`) → faq (`faq`) → others (`list-layout`) → cta (`cta`)
- `/team` **Team** (conditional): intro (`page-intro`) → managing (`team`) → partners (`team`) → associates (`team`) → join (`cta`)
- `/blog` **Insights** (conditional): list (`blog-list`)
- `/contact` **Contact**: intro (`page-intro`) → form (`contact-form`) → office (`map-hours`, conditional)

Looks: sober serif (theme light, material solid, accent brand, font corporate, density comfortable, radius sharp); ledger navy (theme light, material solid, accent ocean, font editorial, density comfortable, radius default); modern advisory (theme light, material solid, accent graphite, font grotesk, density compact).

Pitfalls:
- Professional advertising rules: many bar associations forbid or restrict advertising, success rates, client lists and testimonials; check the local rules before writing claims or quotes.
- The enquiry form inviting confidential documents before a conflict check; say clearly not to send them yet.
- Matters described so precisely that the client can be identified; anonymise and get consent.
- A fee estimate that reads as a binding offer; label it an estimate, show VAT separately and say what is excluded.
- Missing mandatory registration details (registration number, chamber, tax office) in the footer.
- Partner photos with empty alt text; use each person's name.
- Filing calendars drawn as images; keep dates as real text in reading order.
- Motion in the practice preview that ignores reduced-motion settings.

## public-office

**Public office** — A local public office or municipal service where residents come to get a task done: task-first home with today's opening and waits, a searchable services A–Z, dated announcements and an accessibility statement, with an accessibility toolbar on every page.

- `/` **Home**: a11y-toolbar (`accessibility-toolbar`) → service-notice (`announcement-bar`, optional) → hero (`hero` + `input`) → top-tasks (`list-01`) → announcements (`blog-list`) → figures (`stats-band`, optional) → visit (`map-hours`) → accessibility (`rich-text-section`)
- `/services` **Services A–Z**: intro (`page-intro`) → finder (`filter-bar` + `accordion`)
- `/announcements/[slug]` **Announcement**: intro (`page-intro`) → facts (`description-list`) → what-to-do (`alert` + `steps`) → timeline (`activity-timeline`, optional) → affected (`list-01` + `attachment-list`) → more (`blog-list`)

Looks: civic plain (theme light, material solid, accent ocean, density comfortable, font system, radius sharp); institutional (theme light, material solid, accent graphite, density comfortable, font corporate).

Pitfalls:
- Announcements dated or typed by colour only; print dates and types as text.
- An accessibility toolbar that only resizes some blocks or overflows layouts; apply it through tokens so everything reflows.
- No accessibility statement or no way to request an alternative format.
- Live waiting times or hours shown without a 'last updated' time, and wrong on holidays.
- Service search that fails on Turkish characters or synonyms (e.g. accented vs plain spelling).
- Official notices only as PDFs; put the key facts and affected areas on the page as text.
- Decorative motion or low-contrast muted text on a site that must serve everyone.

## publication

**Blog or online publication** — A reading site: an editorial magazine or journal with issues, topics and long reads, or an engineering / technical blog with code samples, tags and a keyboard-first post index. Home, the archive and the article page carry it; author and about pages are optional.

- `/` **Home**: masthead (`page-header`) → lead-story (`media-text`, optional) → latest (`blog-list`) → topics-authors (`feature-grid` + `avatar`, optional) → most-read-letter (`list-layout` + `rich-text-section`, optional) → newsletter (`cta`, conditional)
- `/blog` **Archive**: intro (`page-intro`) → filters (`filter-bar` + `input`) → results (`blog-list` + `pagination`)
- `/blog/[slug]` **Article**: header (`article-layout`) → progress (`reading-progress`, optional) → body (`article-layout` + `rich-text-section`) → author (`avatar` + `card`) → related (`blog-list`) → newsletter (`cta`, conditional)
- `/about` **About** (conditional): intro (`page-intro`) → team (`team`, conditional) → policy (`rich-text-section`, optional) → contact (`contact-form`, conditional)

Pitfalls:
- Images without real alt text or photo credits; covers reused across pieces.
- Missing published and updated dates, author and reading time; these are also what search engines and readers look for.
- Archive filters that reset on back / forward or cannot be linked; keep them in the URL and announce result counts.
- Keyboard shortcuts that fire while typing in a field, or that are not documented on the page.
- Code blocks that break the layout on phones; they must scroll inside their own box and stay readable in both themes.
- Line length too long for reading; keep the body column near 60–75 characters.
- Signup forms without consent wording or a privacy link.

Looks: bright city agency (theme light, material glass, accent ember, font corporate, density comfortable, radius default); private office (theme light, material glass, accent brand, font editorial, density comfortable, radius round).

Pitfalls:
- Listings without the legally required details (agency authorisation number, the owner's written authorisation to advertise, accurate size and price); some markets fine misleading listings.
- Stale listings: sold or let homes left online; every listing needs a status and a listed date.
- Empty or generic photo alt text; describe each room.
- Showing the exact address or unit of an occupied home without the owner's consent.
- A mortgage calculator that reads like a credit offer; label it indicative and date the rate.
- Map-only interfaces: pins must be keyboard buttons and every listing also reachable in the list.
- Autoplaying hero films without a pause control and without a reduced-motion fallback.
- Area price figures without a source and period.

## school

**School & training provider** — A school or training provider (preschool, nursery, driving school, language or skills course) with programmes or courses, a schedule, fees, teachers and an enrolment or sign-up flow.

- `/` **Home**: hero (`hero`) → figures (`stats-band`) → rhythm (`tabs` + `activity-timeline`, conditional) → programmes (`feature-grid`) → how (`steps`) → team (`team`, conditional) → testimonials (`testimonials`, optional, conditional) → fees (`pricing-table`, conditional) → visit (`map-hours`) → faq (`faq`, conditional) → cta (`cta`)
- `/programmes` **Programmes & courses**: intro (`page-intro`) → compare (`comparison-table` + `slider` + `radio-group`, conditional) → groups (`tabs` + `activity-timeline`, conditional) → terms (`table`) → bring (`feature-grid`, optional) → fees (`pricing-table`, conditional)
- `/enrol` **Enrol** (conditional): intro (`page-intro`) → form (`multi-step-form` + `stepper`)

Looks: soft playful (theme light, material glass, accent ocean, density comfortable, font grotesk, radius round); signal grotesk (theme light, material glass, accent ember, density comfortable, font grotesk, radius default); calm institutional (theme light, material solid, accent graphite, density comfortable, font corporate).

Pitfalls:
- Photos of children without parental consent, or identifiable faces and names.
- Collecting more child data than needed, or without a privacy notice for parents.
- Fees shown without what is included, the billing period, tax or extra exam fees.
- Pass rates or results without period and source.
- Timelines and live markers that only work with animation or as a wide graphic; keep a static text version.
- Age and licence requirements only checked after submission; state them up front and next to the field.
- Choices made on the course comparison lost on the way to the sign-up form.

## software-product

**Software product** — Marketing site for a launched software product sold by subscription: a product-led home with a live or scripted demo, proof, features, setup steps and pricing, plus a pricing page, an optional integrations catalogue, a security / data-handling page and a release-notes page. Covers a general B2B app, a data / analytics product and an AI product through alternatives and optional sections.

- `/` **Home**: release-notice (`announcement-bar`, optional) → hero (`hero`) → customers (`logo-strip`, optional) → features (`feature-grid`) → deep-dive (`media-text`, optional) → numbers (`stats-band`, optional) → capabilities (`feature-grid`, optional) → integrations (`logo-strip`, optional) → setup (`steps`) → security-teaser (`media-text`, optional) → quote (`testimonials`, conditional) → pricing (`pricing-table`, conditional) → faq (`faq`, conditional) → closing-cta (`cta`)
- `/pricing` **Pricing** (conditional): intro (`page-intro`) → plans (`pricing-table`) → estimator (`slider` + `stat`, optional) → compare (`comparison-table`) → billing-faq (`faq`)
- `/integrations` **Integrations**: intro (`page-intro`) → catalogue (`filter-bar` + `item` + `badge`) → request (`cta`, optional)
- `/security` **Security**: intro (`page-intro`) → flow (`steps`) → retention (`table`) → admin-policy (`rich-text-section`, optional) → subprocessors (`table`) → report (`rich-text-section`) → security-faq (`faq`, optional)
- `/changelog` **What's new**: intro (`page-intro`) → releases (`release-notes`) → closing-cta (`cta`)

Looks: bright editorial glass (theme light, material glass, accent lime, density comfortable, font editorial, radius default); dense dark data (theme dark, material solid, accent ocean, density compact, font corporate, radius sharp); dark AI glass (theme dark, material glass, accent brand, density comfortable, font grotesk).

Pitfalls:
- Figures without a source ("38% fewer" with no survey, size or period) look invented; every stat needs a source line.
- Demos that look like real customer data or make network calls; mark seeded / scripted data as an example and keep it local.
- Interactive demos that only make sense visually: put the key numbers and the result in text and an aria-live region, honour reduced motion, keep controls keyboard reachable.
- Prices shown without tax note, billing period or what happens at the end of the trial; yearly plans without refund terms.
- Customer logos and quotes used without permission, or integration partner logos used against their brand rules.
- AI products that do not say whether customer data trains models, where it is stored and who the subprocessors are.
- Feature names in internal jargon; buyers search for the job ("shared inbox", "revenue dashboard"), not the module name.
- A changelog that is not kept up: a stale announcement bar or last release from a year ago signals a dead product.

## sports-club

**Sports club** — A sports club or amateur team: next match and recent results, league standings, a filterable fixtures and results page with 'Add to calendar', club news, the ground, and memberships.

- `/` **Home**: hero (`hero` + `fixture-list`) → standings (`standings-table`) → news (`blog-list`, optional, conditional) → ground (`media-text`) → membership-cta (`cta`, conditional)
- `/fixtures` **Fixtures & results**: intro (`page-intro`) → board (`fixture-list` + `tabs` + `filter-bar`) → table (`standings-table`)
- `/membership` **Membership** (conditional): intro (`page-intro`) → plans (`pricing-table`) → join (`steps`) → stands (`feature-grid`, optional) → faq (`faq`) → ticket-office (`cta`)

Looks: matchday poster (theme light, material solid, accent brand, density compact, font grotesk, radius sharp); floodlights (theme dark, material solid, accent lime, density compact, font grotesk).

Pitfalls:
- Results and the table go stale after a match; agree who updates them and show the matchday they reflect.
- Win/draw/loss shown only by colour; add W/D/L letters.
- Kick-off times without the time zone, and .ics files with the wrong zone or duration.
- Photos of youth players published without guardian consent.
- Membership prices without saying what is included (cup games, away games) or the instalment terms.
- Huge unfiltered fixture tables on phones; use filters and month groups.

## subscription-box

**Subscription box** — A recurring-delivery brand (coffee, tea, snacks, books, beauty, pet supplies and similar) priced by box size and delivery frequency: this edition's contents, a plan builder with per-delivery and per-unit price, how it works, the suppliers behind it, and gift subscriptions.

- `/` **Home**: hero (`hero`) → this-edition (`feature-grid`) → plans (`pricing-table`, conditional) → how-it-works (`steps`) → suppliers (`feature-grid`, optional) → reviews (`testimonials`, optional, conditional) → faq (`faq`, conditional) → gift-band (`cta`, optional)
- `/plans` **Build your plan**: intro (`page-intro`) → builder (`pricing-table` + `radio-group`)
- `/gift` **Gift a subscription**: intro (`page-intro`) → gift-form (`form-02` + `date-picker`)
- `/checkout` **Checkout**: checkout (`checkout-01`)
- `/order/[id]` **Subscription confirmed**: confirmation (`order-confirmation-01`)

Looks: warm label print (theme light, material solid, accent ember, density comfortable, font editorial, radius default); playful bright (theme light, material solid, accent rose, density comfortable, font grotesk, radius round); calm curated (theme light, material glass, accent graphite, density comfortable, font editorial, radius default).

Pitfalls:
- Recurring charge not stated clearly before payment (amount, frequency, first charge date, how to cancel) — a legal requirement for subscriptions in many markets.
- Cancelling made harder than subscribing; offer online cancel and say so on the plans page.
- Only the per-delivery price shown; show per-unit and per-month too so plans compare honestly.
- Price grid cells that are not keyboard-operable or not announced with their row and column.
- Current edition section left stale after the cycle changes.
- Gift subscriptions that renew automatically without the buyer knowing.
- Next delivery dates computed in the visitor's time zone instead of the warehouse's.

## venue

**Event venue** — A venue that hires out rooms for weddings, conferences and parties: capacities by layout and head count, the spaces in detail, what is included, viewings, and an enquiry form with a live hire estimate.

- `/` **Home**: hero (`hero`) → finder (`capacity-finder`) → history (`activity-timeline`, optional, conditional) → included (`feature-grid`) → testimonials (`testimonials`, optional, conditional) → visit (`map-hours`) → faq (`faq`, conditional) → cta (`cta`)
- `/spaces` **Spaces**: intro (`page-intro`) → all-spaces (`capacity-finder` + `entity-card`)
- `/enquiry` **Enquiry** (conditional): intro (`page-intro`) → form (`form-01` + `date-picker` + `radio-group`)

Looks: heritage serif (theme light, material solid, accent ember, density compact, font editorial, radius sharp); modern event space (theme dark, material solid, accent graphite, density comfortable, font grotesk).

Pitfalls:
- The site plan is the only source of which rooms fit; list fitting rooms as text too.
- The hire estimate reads like a quote; label it as an estimate and say what it excludes.
- Capacities given without the layout (a room seats far fewer at a banquet than standing).
- Outdoor spaces shown without their seasonal or weather limits.
- Catering and curfew rules hidden until the enquiry, causing wasted viewings.
- Heavy scroll motion without honouring prefers-reduced-motion.
- Choices made in the finder lost when the visitor moves to the enquiry form or switches language.

## wedding

**Wedding or private celebration** — An invitation site for a wedding, engagement or other private celebration: the invitation itself, the couple's story, the programme and practical details (map, travel, where to stay, dress code, gifts, FAQ) and a per-guest RSVP flow.

- `/` **Home**: invitation (`hero`) → countdown (`countdown`, optional) → story (`activity-timeline`, optional) → weekend (`feature-grid`) → venue (`media-text`) → gifts-note (`cta`, optional) → reply (`cta`)
- `/details` **Details**: intro (`page-intro`) → schedule (`activity-timeline`) → map (`map-hours`) → travel-stay (`feature-grid`) → dress (`feature-grid`, optional) → gifts (`rich-text-section`, optional) → faq (`faq`)
- `/rsvp` **RSVP**: intro (`page-intro`) → reply-flow (`multi-step-form` + `stepper` + `radio-group` + `checkbox`)

Looks: stationery serif (theme light, material solid, density comfortable, font editorial, accent lime, radius round); modern minimal (theme light, material solid, density comfortable, font grotesk, accent graphite, radius default).

Pitfalls:
- Guest names and dietary or health details are personal data: keep the RSVP behind the invitation lookup, collect only what is needed and say how long it is kept.
- Letting anyone browse the guest list: the lookup should match one invitation, never list names.
- Dates and times without the day of the week or time zone for travelling guests; the date shown only inside a countdown.
- Plus-ones offered to everyone because the form does not know each invitation's allowance.
- RSVP fields not grouped per guest, so screen-reader users cannot tell whose meal they are choosing.
- Hotel room-block codes and deadlines missing or out of date.
- Heavy animations with no reduced-motion fallback on a site older relatives will open on old phones.
